To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the katanin AAA module cycles between spiral and ring conformations, which is the power stroke for severing.

katanin is the first AAA enzyme whose structure is solved in both spiral and ring forms, that the structure reveals an asymmetric arrangement of AAA domains that is critical for microtubules severing, and that the spiral and ring conformations are interconverted by ATP binding and hydrolysis, providing the power stroke for severing.

we solved a crystal structure and cryo-ET reconstructions of the microtubule-cutting enzyme katanin, which reveal a spiral-to-ring conformational cycle that is likely the mechanism by which katanin cuts microtubules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how microtubule (MT) severing enzymes such as katanin, fidgetin and spastin are regulated to control the length of MTs in cells.
the structure and mechanism of action of microtubule (MT) severing enzymes, which are essential for the biogenesis, maintenance and function of complex MT arrays in axons and cilia.
the molecular mechanism of microtubule (MT) severing, a key step in MT organization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structures of the AAA katanin and spastin enzymes reveal a unique asymmetric architecture that is critical for their function and provide insights into their mechanism of microtubule cleavage.

our work provides a structural framework to understand the mechanism of microtubule seving by katanin, which will help us to design better inhibitors for this enzyme and to understand the role of this enzyme in neurodegeneration.
the katanin hexamer is a molecular motor that cycles between open spiral, closed ring and intermediate states, depending on the nucleotide occupancy of a gating AAA domain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have discovered a new mechanism for the action of microtubule ATPases and that we have solved the structure of a key component in the mechanism.
the structures of microtubule-binding AAA ATPases provide a framework for the mechanism of microtubular action and the basis of a unified mechanism for microtubular severing.

we have solved the structure of the AAA katanin from C. elegans in both monomer and hexamer forms and we have used cryo-EM to determine the conformation of the hexamer when it is bound to ATP and ADP.
The main takeaway from our work is that

katanin and other AAA enzymes involved in severing or disassembly of microtubules and actin filaments have a power stroke that is distinct from the power stroke of AAA enzymes involved in degradation of ubiquitinated proteins.
katanin and spastin are unique among AAA ATPases in that they have a gating protomer, which is essential for their function.
microtubule binding by the katanin module induces a large conformational change that is coupled with ATP hydrolysis.
